author: NPR Politics

title: House Republicans Elect Jim Jordan as Minority Leader
content: House Republican lawmakers have elected Ohio Representative Jim Jordan as their next minority leader. Jordan, a co-founder of the Freedom Caucus, will succeed Mike Johnson as the top Republican in the chamber.
summary: House GOP lawmakers have chosen Ohio's Jim Jordan to serve as minority leader. He will succeed Mike Johnson as the chamber's top Republican.
author: NPR Politics

title: Digitally supported care model improves serum urate target attainment in gout
content: A study published online on November 4 in Arthritis & Rheumatology indicates that a physician-supervised treat-to-target care model improves serum urate target attainment for patients with gout.
summary: A study published in Arthritis & Rheumatology found that a physician-supervised treat-to-target care model improves serum urate target attainment for gout patients. The research was published online on Nov. 4.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Tsukuba researchers propose three-tiered model for PRMT immune regulation
content: Researchers at the University of Tsukuba have proposed a "three-tiered proteostasis model" to describe immune regulation by protein arginine methyltransferases (PRMTs). This framework integrates emerging evidence linking PRMTs to immune regulation, metabolism, vascular function, and age-associated inflammation. The model comprises protein arginine methylation, free methylarginine generation from protein turnover, and methyltransferase-independent interactions with RNA and proteins.
summary: University of Tsukuba researchers have proposed a three-tiered proteostasis model to describe immune regulation by protein arginine methyltransferases. The framework integrates evidence linking these enzymes to immune regulation, metabolism, vascular function, and age-associated inflammation.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Preliminary study links long-term vaping to persistent lung function changes
content:
Preliminary findings published in the journal Tobacco Control suggest that long-term vaping among young people may cause persistent changes in lung function. The researchers note that these cumulative effects could increase the risk of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), a condition characterized by the loss of lung function and a decline in forced expiratory volume in the first second (FEV1).

The study emphasizes that further research is required to confirm these initial observations. While the data links vaping to potential long-term respiratory issues, the authors stress the need for additional investigation to fully understand the extent of these effects.
summary: Preliminary findings published in Tobacco Control suggest that long-term vaping in young people may cause persistent changes in lung function. Researchers warn these cumulative effects could increase the risk of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, though further research is needed.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Case study shows deaf patient denied reasonable adjustments in NHS hospital
content:
An illustrative case history published in the online journal BMJ Case Reports suggests that deaf patients receive inadequate care in NHS hospitals. The account details a deaf inpatient’s experience, highlighting that reasonable adjustments required by U.K. Disability legislation were not implemented during his stay.

The report identifies specific failures in the hospital’s response to the patient’s needs. The necessity for a professional British Sign Language interpreter was not recognized promptly enough, and frontline staff lacked adequate training in supporting deaf individuals. These issues resulted in a lack of proper access to services for the patient.
summary: An illustrative case history of a deaf person's inpatient experience was published in the online journal BMJ Case Reports. The report says reasonable adjustments required by UK disability legislation were not made, a professional British Sign Language interpreter was not recognized promptly, and frontline staff were not adequately trained to support him.
author: Medical Xpress

title: UK food regulations flag only half of processed products as unhealthy
content:
Research published in BMJ Medicine indicates that current U.K. regulatory systems for food and drink identify only about half of processed and ultraprocessed products as unhealthy, defined by excess fat, salt, sugar, and energy density. In contrast, a new nutrient profiling method based on official U.K. Dietary guidance classifies more than 90% of these products as unhealthy.

The researchers suggest that a single unified regulatory system using agreed definitions and aligned with this guidance may offer the best way forward.
summary: Research in BMJ Medicine found that current UK regulatory systems identify only about half of processed and ultraprocessed products as unhealthy. The study notes that new nutrient profiling based on official UK dietary guidance classifies more than 90% of these products as unhealthy.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Study identifies antidepressants that get patients well and keep them well
content: An international research team has investigated which antidepressants can both treat depression and prevent relapse. The study addresses the fact that nearly 6% of the global population experiences depression, with many patients continuing medication after initial improvement to sustain their response.
summary: An international team of researchers investigated which antidepressants can achieve sustained response in patients. This study addresses the need to prevent depression relapse among the nearly 6% of people worldwide who experience the condition.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Trump FCC nominee Thumann faces Democratic scrutiny over Carr's press actions
content: Senators pressured Danielle Thumann, senior counsel to FCC chair Brendan Carr, to speak about agency’s actions toward ABC and Jimmy Kimmel During a contentious Tuesday hearing on her nomination by Donald Trump to serve as a Federal Communications Commission (FCC) commissioner, Senate Democrats hammered Danielle Thumann about recent actions taken by the Brendan Carr-led regulator that have been criticized as hostile to press freedom. Thumann, who serves as senior counsel to Carr, is expected to be approved as commissioner, with Republicans in charge of the US Senate and House. But Ben Ray Luján, a senator of New Mexico, assured her that the commission’s actions will be under close scrutiny when Democrats take charge of the chamber in January.
summary: Senate Democrats pressured FCC commissioner nominee Danielle Thumann to address agency actions toward ABC and Jimmy Kimmel. Senator Ben Ray Luján stated that the commission's actions will be under close scrutiny when Democrats take charge of the chamber in January.
author: Guardian Business

title: Study finds lowest reoffending risk scores preserve accuracy
content:
Ashwin Singh from TU Wien and Carlos Castillo from ICREA/Universitat Pompeu Fabra suggest that when multiple equally reliable computational models yield different recidivism risk ratings, the lowest value should be selected for the individual. This approach aims to preserve overall accuracy in assessing the likelihood of reoffending after prison release.

The researchers note that both human experts and machine learning models consider various factors when evaluating rehabilitation and reoffending risks. Their analysis indicates that choosing the lowest score among equally reliable models is a recommended method for handling discrepancies in risk assessments.
summary: Researchers suggest that when multiple reliable computational models produce different risk ratings, the lowest value should be used for the individual. This approach is proposed by Ashwin Singh and Carlos Castillo to preserve overall accuracy in recidivism assessments.
author: Phys.org

title: Water molecules act as messengers to enable magnetism between metal ions
content: A new study led by researchers at Tohoku University's Institute of Multidisciplinary Research for Advanced Materials, in collaboration with National Taipei University of Technology, reveals that water molecules can act as magnetic messengers. The research demonstrates that tiny shifts in the orientation of these molecules can activate magnetic partnerships between metal ions that are not directly bonded to one another. This finding challenges the conventional view of water as a non-magnetic material by highlighting its role in mediating magnetic interactions through subtle structural changes.
summary: A study by Tohoku University and Taipei Tech found that shifts in water molecule orientation can trigger magnetic partnerships between metal ions. This discovery shows water molecules can facilitate magnetism even when the metal ions are not directly bonded.
author: Phys.org

title: Texas A&M Researchers Upgrade Microscopy to Fivefold Sharper Images While Maintaining Depth
content: Researchers at Texas A&M University have developed a new microscopy technique that resolves structures smaller than 100 nanometers. This method allows scientists to observe fine cellular detail while maintaining the ability to image deep into intact living tissue, addressing a long-standing limitation in biological imaging.
summary: Researchers at Texas A&M University have developed a new microscopy technique that can resolve structures smaller than 100 nanometers, roughly a thousand times thinner than a human hair. The technique allows imaging deep into intact living tissue without sacrificing depth, addressing a long-standing limitation in biological imaging.
author: Phys.org

title: Study finds comparing electricity use with others and tips cuts consumption
content: A new study by Mannheim‑based consumer psychologist Dr. Yavor Paunov and colleagues finds that simple psychological interventions can lower electricity use. The research shows that when people compare their own consumption with that of others and receive practical energy‑saving tips, their overall energy consumption tends to decrease.
summary: A new study by Mannheim-based consumer psychologist Dr. Yavor Paunov and colleagues examined electricity use. The study found that comparing personal consumption with others and providing practical energy‑saving tips can reduce electricity consumption.
author: Phys.org

title: The PlayStation Plus PC app is shutting down next month
content:
Sony is set to retire the PlayStation Plus app for PC on December 10th, ending its cloud streaming feature for the platform. The company announced that it will directly notify users regarding the shutdown.

Sony stated that fewer than 0.4% of eligible PlayStation Plus Premium members were using the PC streaming perk. The company explained that this change allows it to focus on enhancing high-quality experiences that a larger portion of its members prefer to use.
summary: Sony is retiring the PlayStation Plus app for PC on December 10th. Sony says it will notify users directly about the shutdown.
author: The Verge

title: November Pixel Drop brings new icon styles and Gemini AI features to Pixel 10
content:
Google has released the November Pixel Drop, a quarterly update for its Pixel phones that introduces new interface elements and expands AI capabilities. This update includes new icon styles and a feature called Create My Widget. A significant portion of the release focuses on extending Gemini features, previously limited to the Pixel 11, to the Pixel 10 lineup. Notably, the budget-oriented Pixel 10a is excluded from this expansion of AI tools.

The Pixel 10 series will receive improved personalized suggestions, formerly known as Magic Cue, which debuted on the Pixel 11. This feature allows users to send grocery lists to Google Keep from other applications and generate summaries via the context menu. Additionally, Rambler, Google’s AI-assisted voice input system, is coming to the 2025 phones with this update.

Gemini app automation is also rolling out to the Pixel 10 with the November Pixel Drop. This functionality remains restricted to select applications within specific categories, including rideshare, food delivery, and travel. The update follows Google’s introduction of "Gemini Intelligence" branding with the Pixel 11, a designation expected to become more common in future releases.
summary: The November Pixel Drop update introduces new icon styles and the Create My Widget feature to Google's Pixel phones. It also expands Gemini AI capabilities, including personalized suggestions and voice input, to the Pixel 10 lineup while excluding the Pixel 10a.
author: Ars Technica

title: Google Fi adds second 5G network support without naming carrier
content:
Google has announced a “super network” upgrade for its Fi cell service, adding support for a second 5G network. While Google Fi has operated exclusively on the T-Mobile network in the United States for the past few years, this update returns the service to a dual-carrier model domestically. The company stated that connected phones will be able to switch between T-Mobile 5G and another 5G network to optimize connectivity.

Notably, Google has not disclosed the identity of the second network. A blog post announcing the change described the service as supporting “two of America’s best 5G cellular networks” without naming the specific carrier. This marks a shift from the service’s previous configuration following the T-Mobile absorption of Sprint, which had reduced Fi to a single-network service in the U.S., though it continued to hop between networks for international travel.
summary: Google has announced a "super network" upgrade that allows its Fi service to switch between T-Mobile and an unnamed second 5G network. The company stated that this dual-carrier setup will provide better connectivity but refused to identify the specific partner network.
author: Ars Technica

title: Grok Build coding agent leaks confidential data from SpaceXSI and users
content:
Grok Build, a vibe-coding agent developed by SpaceXSI, is leaking confidential data from thousands of users, including proprietary business information and sensitive secrets from the company itself, according to new research. The vulnerability exists because links used to share apps allow access to stored data. Although Grok randomizes URLs to restrict access to those knowing the exact link, a design flaw enables anyone to enumerate thousands of live projects. In most cases, clicking these links opens the app and reveals all associated data.

Research from security firm Claroc indicates the exposed information includes internal business plans, ad proposals, medical exam results, galley checklists from a celebrity cruise line, and employee names and ID numbers. Notably, two-dozen of the affected apps were built by SpaceXSI, the merged entity of SpaceX and xAI.

Among the sensitive documents revealed in the SpaceXSI apps are an onboarding plan marked confidential for a new enterprise sales team member, a sales territory map covering 594 accounts, internal system addresses for sales tools, and various advertising proposals.
summary: Security firm Claroc found that Grok Build's URL design allows anyone to enumerate and access thousands of live projects, exposing proprietary business information and sensitive secrets. The leaked data includes SpaceXSI internal documents such as sales territory maps and confidential onboarding plans, as well as user data like medical exam results.
author: Ars Technica

title: Senate Democrats oppose FCC nominee, plan probes of Chairman Carr
content:
Senate Democrats have opposed President Trump’s nominee, Danielle Thumann Severs, for an open Federal Communications Commission seat. The opposition stems from the timing of the confirmation process, which is occurring during the lame-duck session before Democrats are set to take control of Congress in January 2027. Additionally, Democrats announced plans to utilize their upcoming majority to launch investigations into FCC Chairman Brendan Carr.

At the Commerce Committee’s nomination hearing, Sen. Ed Markey (D-Mass.) stated that there is no justification for advancing partisan nominees during this period, citing the recent rejection of the MAGA agenda by the American people. Thumann Severs, who serves as an attorney and senior counsel to Chairman Carr, faced questioning from Democratic senators regarding her support for Carr’s actions against TV broadcasters.
summary: Senate Democrats opposed President Trump's nominee for an open Federal Communications Commission seat during the lame-duck period. They also announced plans to use their majority next year to launch probes of FCC Chairman Brendan Carr.
author: Ars Technica

title: Amazon unveils AI-powered Ring Drone Cam and Rover Cam for home security
content:
Amazon has announced two new Ring Robotic products, the Ring Rover Cam and the Ring Drone Cam, which are scheduled to reach customers at the end of 2026 and in early 2027, respectively. The announcement, posted on November 10, details that these AI-powered devices are designed to patrol homes and offices. Amazon notes that the introduction of these mobile security cameras is expected to heighten privacy concerns that were previously associated with the company’s earlier attempts to popularize flying security cameras.

The devices operate using an AI Pilot system that integrates cameras, on-device sensors, and cloud processing. This technology allows the units to autonomously navigate around obstacles, such as furniture, while planning patrol routes. Additionally, the AI Pilot system utilizes the devices to digitally map the floor plan of a customer’s property. This mapping process is initiated after a customer carries the Ring drone through indoor spaces or allows the Ring Rover to perform autonomous exploration.
summary: Amazon announced the Ring Rover Cam and Ring Drone Cam, which use an AI Pilot system to autonomously patrol and map indoor spaces. The devices are scheduled to reach customers starting at the end of 2026 and in early 2027.
author: Ars Technica

title: US military gives $150M loans to Stoke Space and Rocket Lab amid Falcon retirement
content:
The US military is implementing a new strategy to support commercial launch companies, a move that suggests defense officials view the potential retirement of SpaceX’s Falcon rocket program as a national security concern. The Pentagon’s Office of Strategic Capital (OSC) has recently announced financial assistance for two SpaceX competitors. On October 26, the office committed a $150 million conditional loan to Stoke Space, followed by a second $150 million loan to Rocket Lab announced on Tuesday.

Stoke Space and Rocket Lab are the first launch companies to receive significant funding from the OSC, an organization created in 2022 to provide capital to firms developing critical national security technologies. Beyond the launch sector, the OSC has been active in recent weeks, committing hundreds of millions of dollars to companies specializing in batteries, drones, and semiconductors. In the space industry specifically, the office also issued a $150 million loan to LeoLabs, a commercial satellite tracking firm, to support the production and deployment of radar units.
summary: The Pentagon's Office of Strategic Capital announced $150 million conditional loan commitments to Stoke Space on October 26 and to Rocket Lab on Tuesday to support commercial launch companies amid SpaceX's planned Falcon rocket retirement. The moves reflect defense officials' view that the retirement could pose a national security risk.
author: Ars Technica

title: OpenAI rolls out new business profiles, making ChatGPT just a little bit more like Google
content: OpenAI has introduced new business profiles to enhance ChatGPT's capabilities as a consumer discovery engine. These features are designed to empower businesses, making the platform somewhat resemble Google's services.
summary: OpenAI rolls out new business profiles, making ChatGPT just a little bit more like Google.
author: TechCrunch

title: Anthropic Founders to Cash Out $250M Each in IPO
content: Each of Anthropic's seven co-founders plans to sell an identical number of shares in the upcoming IPO. At the midpoint of the price range, this transaction would provide each founder with approximately $250 million in cash. Despite these individual sales, the group will retain control of the company.
summary: Each of the seven Anthropic co‑founders will sell the same number of shares in the IPO. The sale would give each about $250 million at the midpoint of the price range and keep the group in control of the company.
author: TechCrunch

title: New York Enforces AI Safety Law on OpenAI and Anthropic
content: New York is set to enforce its new AI safety law, which imposes strict regulatory requirements on large AI developers. The legislation mandates that companies such as OpenAI and Anthropic register with the state, disclose their safety practices, and report any critical incidents. Failure to comply could result in fines.
summary: New York is preparing to enforce its sweeping AI safety law. Major developers such as OpenAI and Anthropic must register, disclose safety practices, and report critical incidents or face fines.
author: TechCrunch

title: OpenAI Acquires Odessia, Travel Startup Founded by Sonder Founder Francis Davidson
content: OpenAI has acquired Odessia, a travel startup founded by Francis Davidson, the creator of Sonder. Davidson is recognized as a prominent figure within the travel industry. OpenAI has not yet disclosed its specific plans for the future of travel.
summary: OpenAI has acquired Odessia, a travel startup, but has not yet announced its plans for the future of travel. The startup was founded by Sonder founder Francis Davidson, a well-known figure in the travel industry.
author: TechCrunch

title: Massie Introduces Eight Impeachment Articles Against Defence Secretary Hegseth
content: Republican Kentucky Congressman Thomas Massie has filed eight articles of impeachment against U.S. Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth. The articles allege violations of the 1973 War Powers Resolution and misconduct related to civilian casualties, as well as operations in Yemen and Venezuela.
summary: Republican Kentucky Congressman Thomas Massie introduced eight articles of impeachment against US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth. The articles allege violations of the 1973 War Powers Resolution and misconduct involving civilian casualties and operations in Yemen and Venezuela.
author: Euronews

title: Democrats Win House, Senate, Leave Republicans with Pride Loss
content: Democrats captured both the House and the Senate and dealt a significant blow to Republican pride last Tuesday night. The piece outlines which parties and individuals benefited from the outcome and which continue to feel the impact this week.
summary: Democrats took the House and Senate on Tuesday night. The article outlines the winners and those still feeling the impact.
author: Euronews

title: Paraguay's new president vows to recover pension funds at risk in Ueno Bank crisis
content: Paraguay’s new president, Pedro Alliana, has pledged to recover pension funds impacted by the intervention in Ueno Bank. The crisis, which resulted in the dismissal of Santiago Peña, has left up to 7,000 people unemployed in Paraguay and abroad. Alliana’s vow focuses on restoring the affected pension assets.
summary: Pedro Alliana, Paraguay’s new president, promises to recover pension funds affected by the intervention in Ueno Bank. The crisis, which led to the dismissal of Santiago Peña, has left up to 7,000 people unemployed in Paraguay and other countries.
author: Euronews

title: Pope Leo XIV draws huge crowds in Córdoba after record Buenos Aires mass
content: After a record Buenos Aires mass, Pope Leo XIV drew huge crowds in Córdoba. Faithful from all over Argentina, from the farthest north to Patagonia in the south, drove hours to attend the service led by the Pope.
summary: Pope Leo XIV led a service in Córdoba that drew huge crowds after a record mass in Buenos Aires. Faithful from all over Argentina, from the far north to Patagonia, drove hours to attend the event.
author: Euronews

title: Pope Leo XIV Celebrates Mass Before 650,000 in Córdoba, Argentina
content:
Pope Leo XIV celebrated Mass before an estimated 650,000 people in Córdoba, Argentina.  

The pontiff greeted crowds from his popemobile before urging worshippers to open their hearts and embrace their faith.
summary: Pope Leo XIV celebrated Mass before an estimated 650,000 people in Córdoba, Argentina. He greeted the crowds from his popemobile and urged worshippers to open their hearts and embrace their faith.
author: Euronews

title: King Felipe VI, Queen Letizia Attend State Funeral for 69 Train Crash Victims in Toledo
content: Spain’s King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia attended a state funeral at Toledo Cathedral on Tuesday, 10 November. The ceremony marked the 69 victims of a high‑speed train collision near Urda on 28 October, during which 69 candles were lit to honor the deceased.
summary: Spain's King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia attended a state funeral at Toledo Cathedral on Tuesday 10 November. The funeral was held for the 69 people killed in a high-speed train collision near Urda on 28 October.
author: Euronews

title: Anthropic plans $1.4 trillion valuation IPO with 825 million shares
content:
Anthropic announced it will offer 825 million shares at $70 to $78 each in its planned IPO, valuing the company at roughly $1.4 trillion.

The IPO is described as a blockbuster, occurring amid investor concerns about risks in the AI boom.

Nvidia also faces pressure over its CEO’s love affair with a suspected Chinese spy.
summary: US firm Anthropic, the company behind the Claude AI chatbot, has announced it will offer 825 million shares at a price between $70 and $78 apiece during its planned IPO. This will give the firm a valuation of around 1.4 trillion dollars.
author: France 24

title: Raphaëlle d’Ornano says Nvidia's central ecosystem role makes any disruption a catastrophe
content:
Erin Ogunkeye welcomed Raphaëlle d’Ornano, Founder and Managing Partner of D’Ornano + Co., to discuss the current state of the AI ecosystem. d’Ornano emphasized that “Nvidia has an absolutely central role in the ecosystem,” adding that “if something happens to Nvidia, it’s going to be a catastrophe.”

When the conversation turned to geopolitics, d’Ornano warned that “there is a real war happening here. It’s an economic war,” describing the competition for frontier AI capabilities as a struggle with profound economic, military, and societal implications. The analysis concluded that the industry is driven by extraordinary technological momentum but is increasingly shaped by concentrated corporate power, geopolitical confrontation, and political resistance to its physical infrastructure.
summary: Raphaëlle d’Ornano says Nvidia's central ecosystem role makes any disruption a catastrophe.
author: France 24

title: Eisenkot pushes October 7 inquiry as Netanyahu targets Arab parties in tense new parliament
content:
Gadi Eisenkot, the politician tasked with forming a new Israeli government, pledged on Tuesday to launch an official inquiry into Hamas's October 7, 2023 attacks and to reverse many of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s policies.

The new parliament was sworn in during a tense opening session in which rival parties traded barbs over the possibility of forming a government with the support of Arab lists.
summary: Gadi Eisenkot pledged on Tuesday to launch an official inquiry into Hamas's October 7, 2023 attacks and reverse many of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's policies. The new parliament was sworn in a tense opening session in which rival parties traded barbs over forming a government with the support of Arab lists.
author: France 24

title: Europe not going anywhere': G7 summit a 'signal to Russians' that Europe is standing behind Ukraine
content: As the US Midterms reshape Ukraine diplomacy, Annette Young is pleased to welcome James Townsend, Atlantic Council's Senior Advisor at the Scowcroft Center's for Transatlantic Security Initiative. "Europe is not going anywhere." With this unequivocal assessment, Townsend, taking place alongside trilateral negotiations in Abu Dhabi. While the latter may command international attention, Townsend argues that the Paris meeting carries a message of its own: European support for Ukraine is intended to remain durable, and Moscow should not mistake diplomatic negotiations for an erosion of Western resolve. The G7 meeting therefore emerges as more than a forum for diplomatic declarations. It represents a test of Western cohesion, the credibility of future military and financial assistance, and Washington's willingness to endorse a common position on Ukraine. As Townsend emphasizes, the final communiqué will also be "a test as far as what Marco Rubio is going to agree to put his name to."
summary: As the US Midterms reshape Ukraine diplomacy, Annette Young is pleased to welcome James Townsend, Atlantic Council's Senior Advisor at the Scowcroft Center's for Transatlantic Security Initiative. "Europe is not going anywhere." With this unequivocal assessment, Townsend, taking place alongside trilateral negotiations in Abu Dhabi.
author: France 24

title: West Bank: MSF reports 3,300 displaced Palestinians and movement limits hinder healthcare
content:
Eve Irvine welcomed Frederica Venturi of Doctors Without Borders (MSF) to discuss ongoing humanitarian challenges in the West Bank.  

Venturi noted that the withdrawal of Israeli forces from Hebron has not ended the crisis. She said about 3,300 Palestinians were forcibly displaced, 15 houses were reportedly demolished, and continuing movement restrictions obstructed access to essential healthcare. Families whose homes were demolished have nowhere to return.  

Hospitals are also reporting shortages of essential medicines, and the movement restrictions during the lockdown prevented medical teams from reaching affected communities.
summary: Frederica Venturi of Doctors Without Borders (MSF) said about 3,300 Palestinians were forcibly displaced and 15 houses were demolished after Israeli forces withdrew from Hebron. She added that ongoing movement restrictions and lockdowns blocked medical teams from reaching communities while hospitals face shortages of essential medicines.
author: France 24

title: US Justice Department charges three Iranian operatives in RAF Fairford terror plot
content: The U.S. Justice Department announced Tuesday that it has charged three men it described as Iranian operatives for an alleged September terrorist plot targeting Britain’s RAF Fairford airbase. Prosecutors said one of the suspects directed others to drive vans, some loaded with fuel barrels, to the base, which hosts U.S. military aircraft and personnel.
summary: The US Justice Department on Tuesday charged three men it described as Iranian operatives for an alleged September terrorist plot at Britain's RAF Fairford airbase. Prosecutors said one suspect directed individuals to drive vans, some carrying fuel barrels, to the base, which housed US military aircraft and personnel.
author: France 24

title: Trump ally Jim Jordan elected House Republican leader, beating Steve Scalise
content: Jim Jordan, a hard‑line ally of former President Donald Trump, was elected House Republican leader on Tuesday after defeating Steve Scalise 106‑73 in a secret ballot, US media reported. He replaces Mike Johnson, who stepped down following Republicans’ loss of both chambers in last week’s midterm elections, and will now lead the party’s opposition.
summary: Jim Jordan, a hardline ally of President Donald Trump, was elected US House Republican leader on Tuesday, defeating Steve Scalise 106-73 in a secret ballot, US media reported. He replaces Mike Johnson after Republicans lost both chambers of Congress in last week’s midterm elections and will lead the party’s opposition.
author: France 24

title: Teddy Riner's presidential bid seen as sign of hunger for alternative to Le Pen, Mélenchon
content:
Teddy Riner, the Olympic judo champion, has announced his intention to run for the French presidency. This move occurs against a backdrop of sociopolitical and economic crises in France, where traditional political parties are struggling to mobilize voters and the political center remains fragmented. Lex Paulson, Director of Executive Programs at UM6P School of Collective Intelligence at Mohammed VI Polytechnic University, discusses the implications of Riner’s entry into the race in an interview with France 24.

Paulson argues that Riner’s candidacy reflects a broader transformation in democratic competition, highlighting the growing importance of personal credibility and public visibility. He notes that in an increasingly fragmented media environment, the ability to capture attention has become a primary political currency, replacing traditional resources like advertising budgets and office infrastructure. Riner’s celebrity status provides him with a significant advantage in this context, offering an alternative to established political elites.

However, Paulson questions whether Riner has articulated a sufficiently developed political vision to be a serious contender, noting that visibility alone does not confer political credibility. While Riner’s public commitments against racism and xenophobia may resonate with voters, the deeper issue lies in what his potential candidacy reveals about the weakness of France’s traditional political alternatives. Paulson suggests that voters increasingly perceive professional politicians as a distant governing class that only listens to citizens during electoral campaigns.

According to Paulson, the central challenge for France’s next generation of leaders is not merely to develop compelling policies but to restore citizens' sense that political institutions are responsive to their lives. He concludes that the real political opportunity lies in reimagining governance by bringing decision-making closer to citizens and giving them a more meaningful voice in the democratic process.
summary: Olympic judo champion Teddy Riner has announced his candidacy for the French presidency. In an interview with France 24, Lex Paulson, Director of Executive Programs at UM6P School of Collective Intelligence, Mohammed VI Polytechnic University, said the bid illustrates voters’ hunger for an alternative to Le Pen or Mélenchon.
author: France 24

title: UK Privy Council overturns Trinidad and Tobago law criminalising male same‑sex relations
content: The UK Privy Council, the last court of appeal for Trinidad and Tobago, has overturned the country’s law that criminalized consensual sexual relations between male same‑sex couples. The decision reflects the colonial legacy that leaves the independent nation’s final appellate authority in London.
summary: A London court has overturned a Trinidad and Tobago law criminalizing consensual sexual relations between male same‑sex couples. As a result of the colonial legacy, it is the independent country's last court of appeal.
author: DW World

title: British police arrest US Army soldier near Gloucester on suspicion of spying for Russia
content: British counterterrorism police arrested a US Army member near Gloucester, England, on suspicion of espionage linked to Russia. Police said he was suspected of espionage activity in connection with Russia, and investigators from the US and UK are involved in the probe.
summary: British counterterrorism police arrested a US Army member near Gloucester, England. Police said he is suspected of espionage activity on behalf of Russia, with US and UK investigators involved in the probe.
author: DW World

title: Climate crisis may push 141 million women into extreme poverty
content: More than one in three women and girls worldwide – roughly 1.5 billion – live in so-called “climate hotspots”, where high exposure to hazards such as cyclones and droughts combine with insecure jobs and deep gender inequality.
summary: The climate crisis could push 141 million additional women into extreme poverty. More than one in three women and girls worldwide, about 1.5 billion, live in climate hotspots with high exposure to cyclones, droughts, insecure jobs and deep gender inequality.
author: UN News

title: UNICEF: Drones up to 1,500 km strike Sudan infrastructure
content: UNICEF said on Tuesday that drones and drought are “closing in” on Sudan, describing unprecedented attacks on the country’s infrastructure. The agency noted that some drones have travelled up to 1,500 kilometres before striking their targets.
summary: UNICEF said on Tuesday that drones and drought are closing in on Sudan. The organization described unprecedented attacks on the country’s infrastructure by drones traveling up to 1,500 kilometres before hitting their target.
author: UN News

title: WHO warns of critical gaps in Africa's health data systems
content:
The World Health Organization has highlighted serious blind spots in Africa’s health data, noting that uncounted deaths can hinder public‑health responses.  

A newly released report points to critical gaps in the continent’s health information systems, underscoring that accurate data are essential for authorities to spot emerging threats and implement lifesaving measures.
summary: A WHO report says quality health data helps authorities detect emerging threats and act quickly. The report finds critical gaps in Africa’s health information systems.
author: UN News

title: UN Security Council meets as South Sudan's first elections approach amid rising violence
content:
The United Nations Security Council convened in New York on Tuesday as South Sudan approaches its first national elections in six weeks since independence. The meeting comes amid deepening political uncertainty and worsening violence across the country.  

Ambassadors are expected to urge an inclusive electoral process and credible polling, while civilians continue to suffer from fighting, hunger and displacement.
summary: South Sudan is about six weeks from its first national elections since independence. The UN Security Council met in New York on Tuesday as ambassadors prepared to press for an inclusive process and credible polls while civilians endure fighting, hunger and displacement.
author: UN News

title: COP31: Energy transition dominates second day as nations plan post‑fossil path
content: During the second day of COP31, the global energy transition was highlighted as nations discussed strategies to leave fossil fuels behind, boost clean energy, and address financial and infrastructure obstacles.
summary: The global energy transition took centre stage on the second day of COP31. Countries explored ways to move away from fossil fuels, accelerate clean energy and address financial and infrastructure barriers.
author: UN News

title: Egypt detains all six Matsadash journalists, UN warns of press freedom assaults
content: Six journalists who constitute the entire newsroom of the Egyptian fact‑checking website Matsadash remain in detention, the United Nations human‑rights office (OHCHR) said on Tuesday. The OHCHR warned that the government’s actions reflect a growing assault on press freedom.

title: 64,000 Flee Violence in Northern Nigeria to Niger as Crisis Deepens
content: Violence in northern Nigeria is driving a regional humanitarian crisis, according to the UN refugee agency (UNHCR) on Tuesday. Since the start of the year, about 64,000 people have fled to neighboring Niger and several hundred have crossed into Benin, with host nations struggling to manage the influx.
summary: Violence in northern Nigeria has forced 64,000 people to flee to neighbouring Niger. Several hundred have also left for Benin, and host countries are struggling to cope, UNHCR said on Tuesday.

title: IOM urges broader Ebola surveillance beyond formal routes in DRC
content: The International Organization for Migration reported that 71 confirmed Ebola cases have been identified along transit routes in the Democratic Republic of the Congo since the outbreak began almost six months ago. IOM called for broader surveillance that extends beyond formal travel pathways.
summary: The International Organization for Migration (IOM) urged wider Ebola surveillance beyond formal routes in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Seventy-one confirmed Ebola cases have been detected along transit routes in the DRC since the outbreak began almost six months ago.

title: US prosecutors indict Mohammad Dawood al‑Saadi for plotting RAF Fairford attack
content:
U.S. federal prosecutors have unsealed an indictment charging Mohammad Dawood al‑Saadi, a dual Iranian‑Iraqi national who is currently in custody in New York, with plotting an attack on the Royal Air Force’s Fairford base in England. The indictment alleges that while detained, al‑Saadi used coded messages in phone calls to his family to convey plans to two co‑conspirators, directing them to purchase large quantities of chemicals that could be used as explosives.

The alleged scheme targeted RAF Fairford, where American B‑1 bombers were stationed, and was foiled before the September attack could be carried out.
summary: US prosecutors indict Mohammad Dawood al‑Saadi for plotting RAF Fairford attack.
author: Guardian World

title: Thomas Markle jailed after cutting off ankle monitor, DOJ says
content:
Thomas Markle, 82, the estranged father of Meghan Markle, the Duchess of Sussex, was arrested in California for possessing child sexual abuse material stored in units. After the arrest, he removed an electronic monitoring device from his ankle.  

The Department of Justice said Markle was jailed following the removal of the ankle bracelet. He remains in custody awaiting a federal hearing in Tampa, Florida, according to first‑assistant U.S. attorney Bill Essayli. Essayli noted Markle was arrested shortly after cutting the bracelet at 1:45 a.m. on Tuesday.
summary: Thomas Markle, the estranged father of Meghan Markle, Duchess of Sussex, was jailed after he cut off his electronic ankle monitor. He had been arrested for keeping child sexual abuse material in California storage units while awaiting a federal hearing in Tampa, Florida, according to first assistant US attorney Bill Essayli.
author: Guardian World

title: Sonia Gandhi’s memoir “Belonging” details personal loss and India’s political divide
content:
Sonia Gandhi’s long‑awaited political memoir, Belonging, has been released. The book provides an insider’s account of India’s political evolution, touching on the assassinations of her husband, Rajiv Gandhi, and her mother‑in‑law, as well as experiences of press stonewalling during Narendra Modi’s tenure.

In the memoir, Gandhi traces her personal journey from a small town in Italy to the highest echelons of Indian power, describing the path as driven by love. The veteran Congress leader, who has previously guarded her private life, says she is opening up for the first time about the extraordinary twists and turns that have unfolded in the public eye.

The Guardian’s Hannah Ellis‑Petersen conducted an in‑person interview with Gandhi about the book, and an excerpt from Belonging is available online. Readers can also sign up for the “This is India” newsletter to receive further updates.
summary: The memoir “Belonging” by veteran Congress leader Sonia Gandhi offers a candid insider’s account of her journey from Italy to India’s highest political echelons. It discusses the assassinations of her husband and mother‑in‑law and press stonewalling under Modi, underscoring a deepening political divide.
author: Guardian World

title: Disgraced former leader Sheikh Hasina plans December return to Bangladesh from exile
content:
Former prime minister Sheikh Hasina, described as a disgraced former leader, faces a death‑penalty sentence in absentia for deaths linked to a 2024 uprising. The ruling indicates she would be subject to that penalty if she returns to Bangladesh.

Party members in exile say Hasina applied for a new passport this week and is “confident” she will return in December. She has lived in self‑imposed exile since August 2024 after being toppled by a mass uprising, crossing into India and remaining in Delhi where she is allowed to live freely.
summary: Sheikh Hasina, a former prime minister, has applied for a new passport and says she is confident she will return to Bangladesh in December. She faces a death penalty after being sentenced in absentia over deaths in the 2024 uprising and has lived in self‑imposed exile in Delhi since crossing into India in August 2024.
author: Guardian World

title: Trump says US war in Iran effectively over and escalation not needed
content: President, after talks with Qatari PM, suggests end to war coming ‘fairly soon’ and military escalation not needed Donald Trump has said that the war in Iran is “effectively over” as he played down concerns that the US would escalate its military campaign against Tehran after the midterm elections. During a White House press conference, Trump said that Israel and Gulf allies in the region were well protected from Iran and that an escalation was not needed.
summary: Trump says US war in Iran effectively over and escalation not needed.

title: Opposition aims to replace Knesset speaker as new parliament sworn in
content:
Israel’s new Knesset will be sworn in on Tuesday, giving opposition politicians their first opportunity to take control of certain levers of power.  The opposition is still working to form a government that could unseat Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.  

A top priority for the opposition is replacing the current speaker, Amir Ohana, who is a close ally of Netanyahu.  The speaker wields significant influence by controlling the legislature’s agenda and committee chairs, making the position a key factor in any attempt to shift power.
summary: Opposition aims to replace Knesset speaker as new parliament sworn in.

title: Israeli opposition seeks new speaker after new Knesset sworn in
content:
Former military chief Gadi Eisenkot has received a mandate to try to form a government, with Netanyahu waiting in case he fails. After Israel’s new Knesset was sworn in, opposition lawmakers quickly deployed their majority to seize control of the legislature from Benjamin Netanyhau and his allies.

The opposition, still too divided to assemble a governing coalition, has asked for a vote on a new Knesset speaker, a role that sets the parliamentary agenda. Replacing Netanyahu loyalist Amir Ohana would allow the six opposition parties to advance key legislation, even if they later broker a coalition.
summary: After Israel’s new Knesset was sworn in, opposition lawmakers used their majority to try to seize control of the legislature from Benjamin Netanyhau and his allies. Although still too divided to form a government, they have asked for a vote to replace speaker Amir Ohana so the six opposition parties can advance legislation.

title: French police arrest individuals after raiding Ritz hotel in Mohamed Al Fayed abuse probe
content:
French police have arrested several people after raiding three properties, including the Ritz hotel in Paris, as part of an inquiry into sexual abuse and trafficking involving Mohamed Al Fayed. The Paris public prosecutor’s office said the individuals were taken into custody for questioning last month and subsequently released.

The operation also included searches of another Paris property and a site in Saint‑Tropez, both described as having links to Al Fayed, carried out in mid‑October.
summary: French police raided three properties, including the Ritz hotel in Paris, as part of an investigation into sexual abuse and trafficking by Mohamed Al Fayed. Several individuals were taken into custody for questioning and later released, and additional searches were carried out at another Paris property and one in Saint‑Tropez in mid‑October.

title: Soul Patrol documentary highlights US Army's first Black special ops team in Vietnam
content:
The documentary Soul Patrol recounts the experiences of the US army’s all-Black Long-Range Reconnaissance Patrol (LURP) during the Vietnam War. This six-man team, composed largely of teenage African American soldiers, operated within Company F 51st Infantry. Their mission involved infiltrating Vietcong enemy lines while carrying 150 pounds of equipment and M16 assault rifles to report on enemy movements. The film, based on the 2003 memoir of the same title by unit member Ed Emanuel, highlights the exceptional bravery these soldiers demonstrated while facing both combat and persistent bigotry.

Emanuel, who transitioned to journalism in civilian life, authored the book based on his own experiences and those of comrades he tracked down. The publication served to encourage other former soldiers to come forward with their stories. The documentary incorporates contemporary home-movie footage and dramatic recreations to depict the unit’s later reunion as older men. One specific anecdote featured in the film describes a panicked unit member who mistook fireflies for a Vietcong insurgent smoking a cigarette in the undergrowth.

The narrative presents the Soul Patrol as an elite special forces unit known for its toughness, capability, and resourcefulness. However, the film also addresses the unit’s experience of racist exploitation, which many members suspected was used to treat them as cannon-fodder. One interviewee describes a near-hallucinatory belief that the enemy had spared them from death in the jungle, seemingly aware of their sacrificial role.
summary: The documentary "Soul Patrol" chronicles the Vietnam War service of the all-Black Long-Range Reconnaissance Patrol unit, which operated behind enemy lines. Based on Ed Emanuel's 2003 memoir, the film depicts the unit's combat experiences and their later reunion as old men.

content: David Walliams, a comedian and former Britain’s Got Talent judge, has been accused of grooming female fans he met when they were as young as 15. The allegations also include harassing women in the workplace over several years. Walliams denies these claims.

title: Former Spurs player Tanvie Hans helps 20,000 Indian women into sport
content:
In 2017, Tanvie Hans, an Indian-born British footballer who played professionally in England, was asked at a dinner party to teach a guest how to play football. She agreed, leading to a Sunday kickabout and the inception of an idea that has since snowballed. Nine years later, Hans and Swetha Subbiah have expanded this initiative to ten cities, bringing sporting sisterhood to a wider audience.

The project, which began from a simple question at a social gathering, has grown significantly over the past decade. The collaboration between Hans and Subbiah has focused on engaging women in sports, culminating in the reported participation of 20,000 Indian women in the program.
summary: Former Spurs player Tanvie Hans and Swetha Subbiah started a movement to get Indian women into sport after a dinner-party request. Their initiative has expanded to 10 cities over nine years.

title: Andreeva 'diva' drama and stopgap finale at Indian Wells bail out WTA
content: Finals have hit California desert after a stormy few years and pre-tournament kerfuffle has added to the fun Towards the end of a positive day for Mirra Andreeva, one of the brightest young stars of women’s tennis, the 19-year-old approached the broadcast cameras to dissect her excellent 6-4, 6-0 win against Elina Svitolina in her first match at this year’s WTA Finals. Andreeva took her place alongside Madison Keys, the 2025 Australian Open champion and a guest reporter for Sky Sports at Indian Wells, who greeted her with a mischievous smile. “Hey, diva!” Keys said. This was an obvious reference to the kerfuffle on the eve of the tournament when Jessica Pegula, known usually as one of the most congenial players on the tour, had been caught on a hot mic delivering a series of stinging criticisms of Andreeva in a private conversation with her coach. Pegula, who had just finished a practice set with an angsty Andreeva, described her rival as a “diva” who “needs to be humbled”. Her comments spread instantly to all corners of the internet.
summary: Jessica Pegula was caught on a hot mic calling Mirra Andreeva a "diva" who "needs to be humbled" before the WTA Finals. The pre-tournament kerfuffle added to the fun as the event hit the California desert after a stormy few years.
author: Guardian Sport

title: F10 unions seek to scrap relegation in Nations Championship
content:
The Six Nations and Sanzaar unions are preparing for a new conflict with World Rugby regarding the potential elimination of relegation from the Nations Championship. This dispute follows the establishment of F10, a new company formed by the 10 leading unions to manage the Nations Championship and handle broadcast and commercial rights for competitions excluding the World Cup.

The F10 unions express concern about financial losses if they were to compete in the second tier. With promotion and relegation scheduled to commence in 2030, some unions are pushing to ensure that none of the top-tier teams face demotion, setting the stage for further negotiations with the global governing body.
summary: The Six Nations and Sanzaar face a new battle with World Rugby as F10 unions seek to prevent relegation from the Nations Championship. The ten leading unions established F10 to manage the competition and its commercial rights, with promotion and relegation set for 2030.

content: Formula One is proceeding with its scheduled season finale in the Middle East, with the Qatar and Abu Dhabi races set to go ahead as planned. Imola, an Italian venue located 20 miles from Bologna, has been stood down as a back-up option for the final race. The Italian circuit had previously been lined up to replace Abu Dhabi due to concerns over the ongoing conflict in the region.
summary: Imola has been stood down as a backup plan for the Formula One season finale as the sport proceeds with its scheduled Middle East races. The Italian venue was previously lined up to replace Abu Dhabi amid concerns over the ongoing conflict in the region.

content:

title: Skagway's 1,100 residents face winter lull after summer cruise boom
content:
Skagway, a coastal town in Alaska with about 1,100 permanent residents, experiences a stark seasonal shift. During the cruise‑ship season, more than a million tourists arrive, filling streets with passengers wearing ship‑name lanyards and prompting shops to stay open and workers to live in crowded bunkhouses.  

When October arrives, the influx recedes: shops are cutting hours or closing, bunkhouse occupants are departing, and the once‑busy streets have dwindled to a trickle of cruise passengers. Snow is now visible on the surrounding mountains as the town settles into winter.
summary: Skagway's 1,100 permanent residents experience a sharp decline in activity as summer cruise ship tourists leave. The town's shops reduce hours and employees depart as the population returns to its baseline.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Fluorescence‑guided nerve imaging faces ambient light challenge in operating rooms
content:
Avoiding accidental nerve damage is a major concern in many surgical procedures. Nerves are hard to distinguish from surrounding tissue, especially in complex anatomical regions.  

Fluorescence‑guided surgery could help by using fluorescent agents that selectively highlight nerve tissue. However, the fluorescence signal is often weak compared with the bright ambient light of an operating room, so surgeons may need to dim or turn off the lights during imaging, interrupting normal workflow.
summary: Avoiding accidental nerve damage is important in many surgeries and nerves can be hard to distinguish from surrounding tissue. Fluorescence‑guided surgery can highlight nerves, but the weak fluorescence signal compared with bright operating‑room lights often forces surgeons to dim or switch off the lights, interrupting workflow.

content: A new study published in the journal Brain Sciences suggests that simple visual tests may serve as an early indicator of cognitive decline, a precursor to dementia.

title: Study links genetic mutation to axonal defects in rare Parkinson's
content: A new study published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences links a genetic mutation associated with Parkinson's disease to abnormalities in a subset of nerve cells. The research provides insights into the causes of the neurodegenerative disorder. D. James Surmeier, Ph.D., the Nathan Smith Davis professor and chair of neuroscience, co-authored the study. He stated that the findings offer new clues regarding how the disease begins and progresses.
summary: A new study in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences found that a genetic mutation linked to Parkinson's disease causes abnormalities in specific nerve cells. The findings provide new insights into how the neurodegenerative disorder begins and progresses, according to co-author D. James Surmeier.

title: Study finds opioid use can become long-term following surgery
content: Claes Gedda of the Department of Clinical Sciences at Danderyd Hospital, Karolinska Institutet, investigated the prevalence of continued opioid use among Swedish patients following surgery. While opioids are effective for managing severe post-surgical pain, prolonged use carries risks of dependence and overdose. Gedda’s thesis examined which patients face a higher risk of long-term usage and evaluated whether opioid use after major surgery can be reduced.
summary: A thesis by Claes Gedda at Karolinska Institutet investigated how common it is for patients in Sweden to continue using opioids after surgery. The research also examined which patients are at higher risk and whether usage following major surgery can be reduced.

title: Oil prices drop to lowest since August after Trump says Iran war is over
content: Brent crude drops below $90 and markets climb after president downplays prospect of further strikes Business live – latest updates Oil prices have fallen to the lowest level since late August while stock markets climbed higher, as markets reacted with relief to Donald Trump saying that the war on Iran is “effectively over”. Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, fell nearly 3% to $89.66, the lowest since 31 August, on Tuesday morning, after the US president downplayed the need for military action against Iran “at this point”. The fall came after a near 6% drop on Monday on signs that the conflict might be nearing an end.

title: US Inflation Climbs 0.4% in October as Gas Prices Drop
content:
New data released after Republicans’ midterms losses – which were largely seen as a rebuke of the party over high prices – shows US inflation rose 0.4% from September to October. The increase was slightly above expectations but still represents a cooldown in price increases, as the cost of gas dipped during the month.

The Bureau of Labor Statistics did not release the usual year‑over‑year inflation figure as part of the consumer price index (CPI), which measures the price of a basket of goods and services, as data was not collected in October 2025 during the government shutdown.
summary: US inflation rose 0.4% from September to October, slightly above expectations, as gas prices fell. The Bureau of Labor Statistics did not release the usual year‑over‑year CPI figure because data was not collected during the government shutdown.

title: Senckenberg researchers uncover cold adaptation mechanisms in Antarctic spiny plunderfish
content:
With water temperatures as low as –1.9 °C (28.6 °F), the Southern Ocean is a place of extreme living conditions. A new study led by Senckenberg researchers shows how fish have adapted to Antarctic temperatures.

The researchers used the Antarctic spiny plunderfish (Harpagifer antarcticus) as a model organism and, for the first time, analyzed the maternal and paternal copies of its genome separately. This allowed them to uncover mechanisms that contribute to this group of fishes' adaptation to extreme cold.
summary: A study led by Senckenberg researchers used the Antarctic spiny plunderfish (Harpagifer antarcticus) to investigate how fish survive in the Southern Ocean's extreme cold. By separately analyzing the maternal and paternal copies of the fish's genome, the researchers uncovered mechanisms that contribute to its adaptation to temperatures as low as -1.9°C.

title: 99‑Million‑Year‑Old Feather Found in Amber Offers Clues to Flight Evolution
content: Long before birds took to the skies, dinosaurs were already sporting feathers. The precise path by which those feathers evolved into the sophisticated structures that enable flight remains unclear. A recent find—the longest feather ever preserved in amber—offers new clues to that evolutionary transition.
summary: Dinosaurs had feathers long before birds took to the skies. The longest feather ever found, a 99‑million‑year‑old feather preserved in amber, provides new clues about the evolution of flight.

summary: Researchers from the University of Johannesburg published a study in Agriculture proposing a policy roadmap for an AI‑driven precision farming approach. content: Neuroscientist Baland Jalal reported waking with a shadowy presence pressing on his chest, an experience that led him to investigate sleep paralysis. In his study, Jalal examines how this frightening condition may shed light on consciousness and the mind‑body connection.
summary: Neuroscientist Baland Jalal woke up feeling a shadowy presence pressing on his chest. He studied sleep paralysis to explain what the condition might reveal about consciousness.

title: Ian Sample discusses seasonal affective disorder with Oxford professor Russell Foster
content:
Ian Sample discusses the latest scientific understanding of seasonal affective disorder (SAD) with Russell Foster, professor of circadian neuroscience at the University of Oxford. The segment explores how darker days impact brain function, noting that while many people experience low mood as nights lengthen, a small proportion develop more intense depression throughout the winter months. This condition, labelled SAD since the 1980s, can be debilitating for those affected.

In the video, Foster explains the potential mechanisms behind the condition and reviews evidence regarding the most effective ways to manage it. The article also provides contact information for crisis support services, including the freephone number 116 123 for Samaritans in the UK and Ireland, the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline in the US, and Lifeline at 13 11 14 in Australia.
summary: Seasonal affective disorder (SAD) is a type of depression that can become more intense during winter months, as explained by Russell Foster, professor of circadian neuroscience at the University of Oxford. The interview with Ian Sample covers the latest scientific understanding of SAD and discusses potential ways to tackle it.
author: Guardian Science

title: Experts warn GLP-1 weight‑loss focus could jeopardize insulin supply
content:
Pharma companies are increasingly prioritising GLP‑1 weight‑loss drugs, a shift that experts say could threaten the supply of insulin. The head of the Access to Medicine Foundation warned that this “gold rush” into products such as Novo Nordisk’s Ozempic and Eli Lilly’s Mounjaro may divert corporate focus from essential diabetes treatments.

GLP‑1 medications have become widespread, with Ozempic and Mounjaro gaining popularity for both obesity and diabetes management. However, many people in poorer countries still struggle to obtain basic diabetes care, including insulin.

According to a report from the Netherlands‑based non‑profit group, the industry’s attention has shifted more toward weight‑loss applications, raising concerns that insulin and other diabetes therapies could receive less emphasis.
summary: The head of the Access to Medicine Foundation says the rush into GLP‑1 weight‑loss drugs may divert attention from diabetes treatments such as insulin. The concern follows the rise of Novo Nordisk’s Ozempic and Eli Lilly’s Mounjaro, which have expanded obesity and diabetes use.

title: NASA CHAPEA Crew Exits 378-Day Isolation at Johnson Space Center
content:
The Crew Health and Performance Exploration Analog (CHAPEA) Mission 2 crew exited their habitat on October 31 after completing 378 days of isolation at NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston. During the simulation, the team arranged photos around a boot print in simulated Martian sand outside their habitat on August 31, 2026.

Health and performance data gathered from this mission will assist NASA in developing strategies to mitigate human spaceflight risks. This research supports future Artemis and Moon Base missions.
summary: The CHAPEA Mission 2 crew exited their habitat at NASA's Johnson Space Center in Houston after 378 days of isolation. Health and performance data from the simulation will help NASA develop methods to counter human spaceflight risks for future Artemis and Moon Base missions.

title: NASA Studies Show LISA Can Detect Exoplanets in Binary White Dwarf Systems
content:
NASA’s latest research demonstrates that the upcoming Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) could identify a new class of exoplanets by detecting subtle changes in gravitational‑wave signals from binary white dwarf stars. Two papers published on Tuesday in The Astrophysical Journal were led by NASA astrophysicist Casey McGrath, a postdoctoral researcher at the University of Maryland, Baltimore County and NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center. The studies show how the presence of a planet orbiting a double white dwarf system would imprint a measurable Doppler modulation on the waves emitted by the tight binary, producing sidebands at frequencies slightly above and below the primary signal.

McGrath’s first paper maps the parameter space in which LISA would be most sensitive. It identifies the planet masses and orbital periods that produce the strongest sideband signatures and estimates that a Jupiter‑mass planet could be detected in such systems out to several thousand light‑years. The second paper, coauthored with Scott Noble and Mary Anne Limbach, explores how the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) could confirm these detections. By measuring the infrared excess produced by a planet in a double white dwarf system, JWST could detect planets as small as five times the mass of Jupiter within a few hundred light‑years, while LISA would be able to find sub‑Jupiter planets under ideal circumstances.

The concept of using gravitational waves to find exoplanets was first proposed in 2008 by Japanese astronomer Naoki Seto. LISA, a joint mission led by the European Space Agency with NASA as a partner, is slated for launch in the mid‑2030s. The observatory will consist of three spacecraft trailing Earth in a triangular formation with sides of 1.6 million miles (2.5 million kilometers). Each craft carries two telescopes that transmit and receive infrared laser beams, allowing the relative distances between the spacecraft to be measured with a precision smaller than the width of a helium atom. These measurements will reveal the passing gravitational waves.

Astronomers estimate that the Milky Way contains about ten million double white dwarf systems with orbital periods of less than an hour, the frequency range that LISA is designed to probe. The mission is expected to resolve roughly ten thousand individual binaries and around one hundred mixed binaries that include white dwarfs, neutron stars, or black holes. Once LISA detects its first exoplanet candidates, the joint observations with JWST will be crucial to confirm that the gravitational‑wave sidebands correspond to real planets rather than false positives.

NASA’s contributions to LISA include the laser system, devices to control electric charge buildup on the proof masses, data‑analysis tools for source identification, and additional scientific and engineering expertise. The agency’s involvement underscores its commitment to using gravitational waves as a new tool for discovering worlds beyond our solar system.
summary: Two new studies led by NASA astrophysicists explain how the LISA observatory can identify exoplanets by detecting gravitational wave signals from tightly orbiting white dwarfs. The research also describes a method for confirming these planets using infrared observations from the James Webb Space Telescope.
author: NASA News

title: NASA Welcomes Expedition 74 Crew Home at Space Center Houston
content:
NASA will host a public event at Space Center Houston on Tuesday, Nov. 17, to welcome home the Expedition 74 crew following their return from the International Space Station. The astronauts and cosmonauts are scheduled to share mission highlights at 6 p.m. CST at the NASA Johnson Space Center’s visitor center. An awards ceremony recognizing key mission contributors will follow the presentation, and the crew members will be available for media interviews prior to the event. Media outlets may request in-person interviews by emailing the JSC Newsroom no later than 5 p.m. on Monday, Nov. 16.

The Expedition 74 team consisted of six individuals who returned to Earth in two separate groups. NASA astronauts Jessica Meir, Jack Hathaway, and Chris Williams, ESA astronaut Sophie Adenot, and Roscosmos cosmonauts Sergey Kud-Sverchkov and Sergei Mikaev comprise the full crew. Williams, Kud-Sverchkov, and Mikaev launched aboard the Soyuz MS-28 spacecraft from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan on Nov. 27, 2025. They returned to Earth on July 26, making a parachute-assisted landing southeast of Dzhezkazgan, Kazakhstan. This 241-day mission, which involved 3,856 orbits and traveled more than 102 million miles, was the first for Williams and Mikaev and the second for Kud-Sverchkov.

Meir, Hathaway, and Adenot launched aboard a Dragon spacecraft on Feb. 13 as part of NASA’s SpaceX Crew-12 mission from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida. After more than seven months in orbit, the trio splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of Los Angeles on Oct. 8. Their 237-day mission included more than 3,792 orbits and traveled over 100 million miles. This was the second mission for Meir and the first for Hathaway and Adenot. Roscosmos cosmonaut Andrey Fedyaev also flew as part of Crew-12 but is unavailable for the upcoming event.

During their time in space, the Expedition 74 crew dedicated more than 1,400 hours to scientific research and technology demonstrations. Their work advanced in-space manufacturing by testing metal and tissue 3D-printing technologies and supported human health studies examining the effects of long-duration spaceflight. Specific research included blood flow studies, assessments of piloting capabilities under changing gravitational conditions, and the activation of a new compact exercise system. The crew also evaluated life-support and environmental systems critical to future exploration missions under NASA’s Artemis program.

Additional scientific efforts included pharmaceutical research to crystalize proteins for cancer medications, advance tumor targeting treatments, and grow stem cells for therapeutics. The crew cared for the first set of plants studied outside of curated systems and upgraded an instrument used to advance the understanding of matter and develop new quantum technologies. They also managed visiting spacecraft and performed essential maintenance to support the continued operation of the orbiting laboratory. Beyond research, the crew engaged students and audiences globally through live educational events, outreach activities, and the sharing of imagery highlighting international collaboration in space.
summary: (March 15, 2026) — The International Space Station orbits 267 miles above a cloudy Atlantic Ocean southwest of Cape Town, South Africa. The Kibo laboratory module’s External Platform and the Canadarm2 robotic arm highlight the top foreground above Earth’s terminator—the line between night and day—in this photograph taken at approximately 6:36 a.

title: Chrome ships Modern Web Guidance 1.0 to help coding agents use native web primitives
content: Browsers natively handle a lot of what used to take 50 lines of JS (or a dependency): `CSS. Highlights` for text range highlighting without s everywhere, ` ` and showModal() give you backdrops and ideal focus management, `field-sizing` to auto-grow textareas as the user types.. (Something yesterday's ftrain post touched on [0]) Models know about some of these by name, but consistently won't default to using the platform-native solution and instead prefer the incumbent +JS based pattern. We started an effort in Chrome to supplement coding agents with this key domain knowledge and we're shipping our 1.0 today, in collaboration with Firefox, MDN, and Edge. 200+ guides (~1.7MB) of curated, hand-crafted implementation best-practices from web experts, updated as the web evolves. (Open source, obv, so.. We'll welcome your bikeshedding ;) Readable versions here: [1] I've spent the last 9 months obsessing over how to ship this as an agent skill + (Agentic RAG) CLI without blowing up your context window. (Or cedeing activation mechanics to MCP dynamic tool search). The skill description is minmaxed for activating on relevant frontend tasks. The RAG work I'm pretty proud of… originally a 500mb native stack down to a ~7MB pure-JS package, ~10ms search on your CPU. We just introduced a deterministic 'legacy-scan' (trained on 30k github repos) to identify old 'n dusted patterns that your agent can modernize. (92% avg precision on held-out repos.) People make a lot of claims about what coding agents are good/bad at. We wanted receipts, so we invested heavily in eval infra [2] to help us hill-climb, but also to identify when knowledge is common enough we can prune our guides. (Ofc, some of the things we thought AI didn't know turned out to be wrong :) We run codex/claude/agy against 200 tasks without the skill and then with.. In total ~1,700 playwright/AST-based assertions. Agents go from 55% pass unguided to 92% guided. Try it out: DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 npx modern-web-guidance@latest install DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 npx modern-web-guidance@latest search "animate dialog modal" DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 npx modern-web-guidance@latest legacy-scan./src If you spot something wrong or weird, give us a holler! Longer write-up on the 1.0: https://developer. Chrome. Com/blog/modern-web-guidance-v1 --- 0: https://news. Ycombinator. Com/item? Id=50416456 1: https://developer. Chrome. Com/docs/modern-web-guidance/guides 2: https://googlechrome. Github. Io/modern-web-guidance-src/ Comments URL: https://news. Ycombinator. Com/item? Id=50443812 Points: 9 # Comments: 1
summary: Chrome ships Modern Web Guidance 1.0 to help coding agents use native web primitives.

title: Outokumpu’s EvoMaterials platform aims to rethink metal extraction
content:
The metals industry has long been shaped by landmark innovations such as the Bessemer process, flash smelting, electric arc furnaces, and modern continuous casting. Despite these breakthroughs, most extraction methods still rely on scientific foundations that have remained largely unchanged for more than a century. Outokumpu, the global leader in sustainable stainless steel and ferrochrome production, is questioning this status quo through its EvoMaterials platform, a technology initiative aimed at rethinking how metals are extracted.

The need for new approaches is driven by a growing demand for critical metals. As economies expand and electrification spreads, data and scientific models show that minerals are required for data centers, aerospace, water treatment, energy systems, and defence. At the same time, many Western economies have reduced domestic processing capacity for the very metals that these industries depend on. Metallurgy is therefore becoming strategically important, with considerations of cost, availability, carbon footprint, geographic origin, and supply‑chain resilience shaping the sector. This is especially true for chromium and other specialty metals used in high‑temperature and extreme‑environment applications.

EvoMaterials originated from research into sulfidation‑based processing technologies, initially pursued to lower the carbon emissions associated with ferrochrome production. Laboratory work revealed that these alternative chemistries could recover valuable metals from lower‑grade resources and industrial side streams while fundamentally altering separation processes. The platform aims to rethink mineral resource use, increase resource efficiency, and strengthen industrial competitiveness.

The technology began in the United States in 2021, processing chromite from Outokumpu’s Kemi mine in Finland—the only chrome mine in the European Union and one of the few such operations in the Western world. Since then, Outokumpu has refined the process through extensive research and development, combining new chemistries with proprietary metallurgical expertise and a non‑exclusive patent license agreement from MIT. The new method creates a different chemical environment that enables more efficient extraction with fewer losses and by‑products, allowing recovery of critical materials from resources previously considered waste.

EvoMaterials is described as a technology platform rather than a single process. Once a new extraction pathway is mastered for one material system, the same scientific principles may be adapted to other metals and mineral resources. The next step is pilot‑scale validation: a plant in New Hampshire will begin operations in the first half of 2027, scaling the technology from laboratory to one‑ton production. The goal is industrial‑scale deployment by 2030, with the potential to produce low‑CO₂ chromium‑enriched ferrochrome and chromium metal, and to adapt the platform to nickel, molybdenum, and other strategic materials. The initiative raises a broader question about whether today’s metallurgical processes could look different if invented from scratch, suggesting that the next revolution in materials may begin by rethinking metal extraction itself.
summary: Outokumpu has developed EvoMaterials, a technology platform that uses sulfidation-based processing to extract metals more efficiently and produce low‑CO2 ferrochrome and chromium metal. A pilot plant in New Hampshire will begin operations in the first half of 2027 to validate the technology.

title: Scott Wiener, Pelosi’s successor, plans to regulate AI amid data center power concerns
content: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. Nancy Pelosi’s replacement is ready to regulate AI —Grace Huckins As a California state senator, Scott Wiener authored legislation aimed at curbing the risks of advanced AI. Now, after winning a tight congressional race for Nancy Pelosi’s open San Francisco seat, he could play a key role in setting federal AI policy. I spoke with Wiener only a few hours after he had been declared the victor. But he was already thinking about AI risk: during our 20-minute conversation, he used the phrase “recursive self-improvement” half a dozen times. “We need to slow this down,” he told me. “Because it’s moving very quickly, and we could sleepwalk into a disaster.” Still, he describes himself as only “cautiously optimistic” about Congress’s ability to rein in AI. Here’s what he plans to do about it. The backlash about data centers might really just be about electricity —James O’Donnell As voters went to the polls across the US last week, I was in Ashburn, Virginia, part of what’s known as Data Center Alley—the world’s largest data center hub. It’s also where the backlash sweeping the country arguably first began to take shape. Big Tech has framed the data center uproar as a culture war over progress. But a few days in Ashburn convinced me the real fault line may be electricity: drawing it from the grid or generating it onsite provokes different forms of blowback. The industry can improve its image, but it can’t escape the consequences of its enormous appetite for electricity. Find out why. This story is from The Algorithm, our weekly AI newsletter. Sign up to receive it in your inbox every Monday. One More Thing China wants to restore the sea with high-tech marine ranches Just a short ferry ride from the Chinese port city of Yantai sits Genghai No. 1, a strange offshore complex that combines a tourist attraction with an industrial fish farm. It even has a seven-story visitor center shaped like a cartoon starfish. But its main purpose is to breed fish and release them into the ocean. Genghai is part of China’s ambitious marine ranching program. Since 2015, the country has built 169 demonstration ranches and released at least 167 billion juvenile fish and shellfish. content:
